entries.answer: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object currently known to support life.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System.
A black hole is a region of spacetime bounded by an event horizon from which signals cannot escape to distant observers.
The Solar System consists of the Sun and objects gravitationally bound to it, including planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
The Milky Way is the barred spiral galaxy that contains the Solar System.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and a terrestrial planet.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System and a gas giant.
Saturn is a gas giant known for its prominent ring system.
Venus is the second planet from the Sun and has a dense carbon-dioxide-rich atmosphere.
Mercury is the smallest and innermost planet of the Solar System.
Neptune is the eighth and most distant recognized planet from the Sun.

aliases: how long does earth orbit sun
entries.answer: Earth completes one orbit around the Sun in about 365.25 days.

aliases: how long does moon orbit earth
entries.answer: The Moon's sidereal orbital period around Earth is about 27.3 days.

aliases: how many moons does mars have
entries.answer: Mars has two known natural satellites, Phobos and Deimos.

aliases: how many moons does jupiter have
entries.answer: Jupiter has many known natural satellites; the exact count can change as new small moons are confirmed.
Saturn has a prominent ring system made mainly of particles of water ice and rocky material.
Venus rotates very slowly and in the opposite direction to most planets.
Mars has a thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide.
An asteroid is a relatively small rocky or metallic Solar System body, many of which orbit the Sun.
A comet is an icy Solar System body that can develop a coma and tail when heated near the Sun.
An exoplanet is a planet outside our Solar System that orbits another star or, in some cases, a stellar remnant.
A light-year is a unit of distance equal to the distance light travels in vacuum in one Julian year.
A parsec is an astronomical unit of distance defined through stellar parallax and equal to about 3.26 light-years.
